claim.supported_scope: Independently implemented graph-defined continuous-outcome OLS path analysis with bounded parallel and serial mediation, continuous or exact-0/1 moderation, bounded moderated mediation, conditional effects, HC3 and Student-t inference, simple slopes, Johnson-Neyman regions, and optional dedicated percentile and conditional-BCa case bootstrap.
claim.estimand: Graph-defined direct, indirect, conditional, and moderated-mediation effects for bounded observed-variable continuous-outcome OLS systems.
assumptions: The authored directed graph is acyclic and all endogenous equations share one listwise-complete continuous-outcome sample.
Each unstandardized OLS equation is full rank and its exact HC3 covariance remains finite and positive on every requested conditional-effect domain.
Case-bootstrap sampling units are exchangeable and at least 90 percent of requested fits are usable when bootstrap inference is requested.
exclusions: Copied numbered PROCESS templates, proprietary macros, and SmartPLS project import or numerical-identity claims are excluded.
Binary endogenous equations, weights, clusters, broader categorical coding, cycles, reciprocal paths, and custom confidence levels or tails are excluded.
Intermediate-stage moderation, multiple moderated edges on one indirect path, and two-moderator products on a mediated path are excluded.
warnings: Observed-variable path coefficients and conditional effects do not by themselves establish causality.
Reference-condition effects must not be described as unconditional when a relevant path is moderated.
Bootstrap BCa output is available only when its complete delete-one acceleration contract passes.

equations.expression: V_HC3 = inverse(X_prime X) X_prime diag((e_i / (1 - h_i))^2) X inverse(X_prime X)

references.citation: MacKinnon and White (1985), Some Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Covariance Matrix Estimators with Improved Finite Sample Properties
Preacher, Curran, and Bauer (2006), Computational Tools for Probing Interactions
Hayes (2015), An Index and Test of Linear Moderated Mediation
Independent Python and R reconstruction of the frozen graph-defined PROCESS v2 arithmetic

simulations.design: Preregistered direct, parallel and serial mediation, one- and two-moderator, and bounded moderated-mediation graphs with known continuous-outcome coefficients.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen indexed data-generation streams and deterministic point estimation.
simulations.acceptance_rule: The dedicated report must satisfy its frozen recovery and coverage boundaries for every advertised graph family.

simulations.design: Rank-deficient equations, near-unit leverage, invalid covariance, degenerate probe grids, unsupported graphs, failed resamples, and incomplete jackknife sets.
simulations.seed_policy: Deterministic named boundary fixtures plus fixed replicate-index-addressed bootstrap streams.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Every invalid case receives the frozen diagnostic, bootstrap failures remain accounted for, and no cancelled or invalid run commits partial analytical output.

boundaries.case: An equation is rank deficient, HC3 leverage is unstable, covariance is invalid, or a requested conditional-effect variance is nonpositive.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The affected analysis fails with its typed diagnostic and no fabricated statistic, interval, or partial result.

boundaries.case: The graph is cyclic, exceeds documented caps, uses an unsupported endogenous family, or contains an unsupported moderation position.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Setup is blocked before estimation and identifies the offending graph feature.

boundaries.case: Variables and graph declarations are consistently reordered without changing their semantic identities.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Canonical mapped equation, path, and conditional-effect outputs remain equal within the frozen tolerance.

boundaries.case: The same graph, dataset, seed, and settings are executed with different supported worker counts.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Replicate identities, failures, effect summaries, and analytical payloads are exactly equal.

boundaries.case: A graph identity, coefficient, covariance, probe token, bootstrap witness, method version, or dataset fingerprint is altered after execution.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict archive validation rejects the entire changed result instead of rendering or exporting it.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject a result whose capability identity differs from its recipe.
Reject a result relabeled as another PROCESS method version.
Reject a result whose saved dataset fingerprint no longer matches.
Reject any modified archive entry whose checksum no longer matches.
Reject duplicated keys, unknown fields, non-finite values, ambiguous effect identities, or inconsistent sufficient statistics.
Never reinterpret regression_process_v1 or unrelated mediation and moderation shells as a current v2 result.

persistence.legacy_policy: Historical regression_process_v1 payloads remain immutable and readable but cannot be executed, appended, or promoted as graph-defined v2 evidence.

setup_controls: Optional bootstrap replicates, seed, and workers
native.gui_cli_parity_rule: For the same graph, dataset, settings, and seed, GUI and CLI analytical payloads must be exactly equal apart from operational timestamps; bootstrap scientific output must also be worker-invariant.
accessibility_rules: Every graph, interaction plot, and Johnson-Neyman display has an equivalent accessible data table.
Effect conditions, unavailable results, exclusions, and warnings are available without color or pointer interaction.
